FailureDatabase.description: Facts about the database a ``database_*`` failure concerns, taken from the readiness error.

database_path.description: The configured target; null for an in-memory database.
database_path.title: Database Path

expected_revision.description: The bundled schema revision, when it could be determined.
expected_revision.title: Expected Revision

FailureDatabase.title: FailureDatabase

FailureDiagnostic.description: One failed historical-quality rule and its sanitized reason.
FailureDiagnostic.title: FailureDiagnostic

FailureReasonCode.description:
Stable failure categories a caller may branch on.

A value is never renamed, repurposed or removed within the public contract. New values may be
added, so a caller must treat an unrecognized value as a generic failure and use ``status`` for the
category.
FailureReasonCode.title: FailureReasonCode

ProviderFailure.description:
Why an analysis outcome is a provider failure: one of three codes and the inputs that caused it.

The same element is carried by the failure envelope and by every document that reports an analysis
outcome. ``reason_code`` is the single code derived from the kinds in ``inputs``.
ProviderFailure.title: ProviderFailure

ProviderFailureInput.description: One failed input: which provider failed it and what the adapter observed.

input.description: The strategy input the failure was recorded against; null when the failure was raised.
input.title: Input

ProviderFailureInput.title: ProviderFailureInput

ProviderFailureKind.description:
What a provider failure was, as observed by the adapter.

``UNREACHABLE``: the service did not serve the request (DNS, connection, timeout, throttling or blocking,
server errors). ``UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE``: the service answered, but not in the form the adapter reads.
``NO_DATA``: the service answered correctly and has nothing for this request.
ProviderFailureKind.title: ProviderFailureKind

description:
The one JSON document written to standard output when a command with ``--json`` fails.

``schema_version`` is this document's own lineage: it identifies a shape only within this schema
and is independent of the ``schema_version`` of every success document. A consumer dispatches on
``status`` and ``result`` first, then on ``analysis``. ``reason_code`` is stable; ``reason`` and
``diagnostics[].reason`` are sentences for people and carry no guarantee.

analysis.description: The analysis of a direct command; null otherwise.
analysis.title: Analysis

database.description: Set only for a database_* code; null otherwise.

method.description: The method of a direct command; null otherwise.
method.title: Method

provider_failure.description: Set exactly when reason_code is one of the three provider failure codes; null otherwise.

result.description: Always null, so success and failure share top-level keys.
result.title: Result

ticker.description: The requested ticker of a direct command; null otherwise.
ticker.title: Ticker

title: FailureEnvelope
